approximation_note: Both engines integrate the random effects out by the ORDINARY LAPLACE approximation for these cases, not AGHQ: the frozen R adapter's `aghq` control defaults to FALSE (Laplace) -- see .unlazy/core070-aghq/oracle-source/readback/R/gllvmTMB.R lines ~1591/2037/2056 ('aghq = FALSE uses the Laplace approximation (the current default)') -- and the Julia side calls `fit_binomial_gllvm` directly, whose marginal is `binomial_marginal_loglik_laplace` (src/families/binomial.jl), the same dense-Laplace kernel used throughout this engine. Because both sides use the identical integral approximation, this is a same-approximation comparison of two INDEPENDENT optimizations (distinct L-BFGS runs from distinct warm starts), matching the paired-independent-fit precedent already established in tests/testthat/test-julia-bridge.R (gllvmTMB lane) and in tools/core070_namespace_2_batch.jl's own tolerance-calibration comment: 1e-4 absolute on logLik and on max|coef delta|, not the 1e-6..1e-8 used for same-point objective-identity checks elsewhere in this repo.
